1. the accommodation of large districts of people.
2. unless those people would relinquish the right of.
3. Representation in the Legislature, a right inestimable to them.
4. and formidable to tyrants only. He has called together legislative.
5. bodies at places unusual, uncomfortable, and.
6. distant from the depository of their public.
7. Records, for the sole purpose of fatiguing them.
8. into compliance with his measures. He has dissolved Representative.
9. Houses repeatedly, for opposing with manly firmness his invasions on.
10. the rights of the people. He.
11. has refused for a long time, after.
12. such dissolutions, to cause others to be elected.
13. whereby the Legislative powers, incapable of Annihilation, have returned.
14. to the People at large for their exercise; the State.
15. remaining in the mean time exposed.
16. to all the dangers of invasion from.
17. without, and convulsions within. He has endeavoured to.
18. prevent the population of these States; for that purpose.
19. obstructing the Laws for Naturalization of Foreigners; refusing to pass.
20. others to encourage their migrations hither.
